editorial:
Ever feel like your life is just a mess and you need a magic fix? That is exactly where you find our main character. She is young, unhappy, and tired of everything going wrong. When she stumbles upon a self-help book called Perfect Thoughts, she thinks she has found the secret map to a better life. The movie has a light, quirky feel to it that makes you root for her as she tries to change her habits and fix her relationships. It is a sweet mix of laughs and real-life struggles that feels very relatable if you have ever tried to turn your life around.

You will love how the acting keeps things grounded so the story does not feel too cheesy. The pacing is steady, though some parts move a bit slow, but the emotional payoff makes it worth it. If you enjoy stories about personal growth and awkward romance, you should definitely give this one a try. Since it is a smaller indie film, you might want to look for it as a digital rental on Apple TV or see if it is streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture. Adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great call if you love these kinds of hidden gems.
endingExplained: By the end, you see that the self-help book was not a magic cure, but a tool to help her face her fears. She stops trying to be perfect and starts being honest with herself and the people she loves. The movie wraps up with her finding a healthy balance in her life and a real connection with a partner. She realizes that happiness comes from acceptance, not from following a set of rules in a book.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about self-discovery and quirky romances.
